sites.name: Kody Riggan Datto Boat Ramp
sites.description: AGFC concrete boat ramp on the main Black River channel in the heart of Dave Donaldson Black River WMA, at the end of County Road 113 south of Datto and Reyno. Heavily used by waterfowl hunters in winter. The parking lot was enlarged in 2017 on land donated by the Riggan family. Put-in for the 6.7-mile lowland float to Brookings Access through bottomland hardwood forest.
sites.facilities: Concrete boat ramp and gravel parking area. No restrooms, water or camping are documented at this access.
sites.parking_info: Gravel AGFC parking area beside the ramp. AGFC marks it mobility-impaired accessible. It was enlarged in 2017 after long-standing crowding, but it can still fill on duck-season mornings.
sites.road_access: From US 62/67 at Reyno (south of Corning), go east on County Road 116 about 2 miles, then turn south on County Road 113 and follow it about 1.5 miles to the road's end at the ramp. AGFC's own directions just say to go south from Corning on Highway 67 to Reyno and watch for the Datto access signs.
sites.fee_notes: No site fee. AGFC requires users 16 and older to carry an Arkansas hunting or fishing license or an annual AGFC WMA/Lake Conservation Permit ($10.50) on Dave Donaldson Black River WMA. This applies to paddling too, effective July 1, 2026.
sites.local_tips:
Dave Donaldson Black River WMA rules apply. Anyone 16 or older without an Arkansas hunting or fishing license needs an AGFC WMA/Lake Conservation Permit (annual, $10.50, required since July 1, 2026; paddling is covered). In duck season, the WMA is closed to all access from 2 to 4 a.m. (Nov. 21-Jan. 31 and Feb. 6-7 in 2026-27), except in designated campsites, parking areas, boat ramps and staging areas. The no-boat periods for the 2026-27 season (Nov. 14-20, Nov. 30-Dec. 9, Dec. 24-25, Feb. 1-5, plus noon to 4 a.m. on most days of the regular season) exempt the Black River channel itself. Waterfowl hunters must be off the water by noon. Camping is allowed only in designated primitive campsites. Expect hunting on the surrounding WMA (deer archery from Sept. 26 to Feb. 28, a permit modern-gun deer hunt Nov. 14-18, and waterfowl).

Busiest at pre-dawn in duck season, when hunters launch in the dark. Floaters should avoid weekday and weekend mornings from late November through January. The Black River near Peach Orchard gauge (USGS 07064026) is about 3 river miles downstream and is the best flow reference for this reach.

AGFC's access-sign point is 17 m away, and the separate AGFC parking feature is 45 m away. On the AGFC public-use map (page 2 of 3), the concrete-ramp symbol sits at the end of County Road 113, on the river bank. Note that OSM tags this channel as an unnamed 'waterway=river'. OSM's 'Black River' main_stream instead follows the channel that NHD and AGFC call Little River, about 2 km east.

sites.name: Brookings Boat Ramp
sites.description: AGFC concrete boat ramp on the Black River at the end of Highway 280 in the Brookings community west of Peach Orchard. It is the main river access to Dave Donaldson Black River WMA. A free, no-hookup AGFC camping area is just up the road. Take-out for the 6.7-mile float from Datto, and put-in for the 11.2-mile float down to Schaeffer's Eddy.
sites.facilities: Concrete boat ramp and gravel parking area. AGFC's primitive Brookings Camping Area (RVs allowed, no hookups, no fee) is about 0.4 mile north. No restrooms or drinking water are documented.
sites.parking_info: Gravel AGFC parking area at the ramp, marked mobility-impaired accessible. Shared with duck hunters and with users of the Brookings moist-soil units and dove field.
sites.road_access: From Delaplaine, take Highway 90 north about 2 miles and turn left onto Highway 280. Follow 280 north about 4 miles to a stop sign, then turn left; the road ends at the Brookings access on the Black River. From Peach Orchard, Highway 280 runs west about a mile to Brookings.
sites.fee_notes: No site or camping fee. Users 16 and older need an Arkansas hunting or fishing license or an annual AGFC WMA/Lake Conservation Permit ($10.50), effective July 1, 2026.
sites.local_tips:
Dave Donaldson Black River WMA rules apply. Anyone 16 or older without an Arkansas hunting or fishing license needs an AGFC WMA/Lake Conservation Permit (annual, $10.50, required since July 1, 2026; paddling is covered). In duck season, the WMA is closed to all access from 2 to 4 a.m. (Nov. 21-Jan. 31 and Feb. 6-7 in 2026-27), except in designated campsites, parking areas, boat ramps and staging areas. The no-boat periods for the 2026-27 season (Nov. 14-20, Nov. 30-Dec. 9, Dec. 24-25, Feb. 1-5, plus noon to 4 a.m. on most days of the regular season) exempt the Black River channel itself. Waterfowl hunters must be off the water by noon. Camping is allowed only in designated primitive campsites. Motorized boats are prohibited on the nearby Brookings GTR from Nov. 14 to Feb. 7, and the Brookings moist-soil units are closed to entry from Nov. 1 to Feb. 15. Neither restriction applies to the river. A permit dove hunt is held at Brookings Field on opening weekend (Sept. 5-6, 2026).

In a major flood, Brookings itself goes under: NWS says the community floods at about 17 ft on the Black River at Corning gauge, where flood stage is 15 ft. The AGFC area residence is next to the access.

sites.name: Schaeffer's Eddy Boat Ramp
sites.description: AGFC concrete boat ramp and paved parking lot on the lower Black River at the south-west end of Dave Donaldson Black River WMA, at the end of Hite Road south of Biggers. Take-out for the 11.2-mile float from Brookings. The site is also a signed archaeological site, so leave artifacts where they lie. The Current River joins the Black about 17 river miles below here.
sites.facilities: Concrete boat ramp and paved parking lot. No restrooms, water or camping are documented in AGFC data.
sites.parking_info: Paved AGFC parking lot at the ramp, marked mobility-impaired accessible.
sites.road_access: From US 62/67 at the south edge of Biggers, take Hite Road south. It jogs west briefly on Lutrell Cemetery Road, then continues south. Follow it to its end at the river, about 3 miles in all; the final stretch is the county-maintained Schaeffer's Eddy road.
sites.fee_notes: No site fee. Users 16 and older need an Arkansas hunting or fishing license or an annual AGFC WMA/Lake Conservation Permit ($10.50), effective July 1, 2026.
sites.local_tips:
Dave Donaldson Black River WMA rules apply. Anyone 16 or older without an Arkansas hunting or fishing license needs an AGFC WMA/Lake Conservation Permit (annual, $10.50, required since July 1, 2026; paddling is covered). In duck season, the WMA is closed to all access from 2 to 4 a.m. (Nov. 21-Jan. 31 and Feb. 6-7 in 2026-27), except in designated campsites, parking areas, boat ramps and staging areas. The no-boat periods for the 2026-27 season (Nov. 14-20, Nov. 30-Dec. 9, Dec. 24-25, Feb. 1-5, plus noon to 4 a.m. on most days of the regular season) exempt the Black River channel itself. Waterfowl hunters must be off the water by noon. Camping is allowed only in designated primitive campsites. The access is a signed archaeological site: do not dig or collect artifacts.

The WMA master plan says duck hunters use this ramp and Brookings to reach the Winchester GTR with a two-boat system, so expect hunter traffic in the dark on winter mornings. The area south-west of the ramp often floods in summer from agricultural irrigation runoff.

sites.name: Dan River Access
sites.description: MDC-managed 68-acre access on the Black River about 5 miles southeast of Poplar Bluff. Concrete boat ramp on the main channel with a gravel parking lot, privy and disabled-accessible facilities. Below Poplar Bluff the Black is a slow, sandy lowland river between levees. This is the first public ramp downstream of Sportsman's Park, about 8 river miles. Walk-in or float-in camping is allowed.
sites.facilities: Concrete boat ramp, parking lot, privy, disabled-accessible facilities (per MDC area map and ramp layer). Open walk-in/float-in camping. No other developed facilities listed.
sites.parking_info: Parking lot next to the ramp at the end of the gravel access road. In aerial imagery it is a long gravel lot (roughly 80 m) with room to turn trailers. MDC does not publish a capacity.
sites.road_access: From Poplar Bluff, take Highway 53 southeast 3.9 miles, turn left (east) on County Road 616 for 1.0 mile, then turn left (north) on County Road 611 for 0.7 mile to the area. The access road continues to the parking lot and ramp.
sites.fee_notes: No fee is listed on the MDC area page. MDC conservation areas and accesses do not charge entry fees.
sites.local_tips: Area open 4 a.m. to 10 p.m. Launching and landing boats, fishing and camping are allowed 24 hours. Watercraft and commercial vehicles may not be parked or stored during closed hours. Camping is limited to walk-in/float-in/backpack open camping (14 consecutive days in any 30-day period). Pets must be leashed. No target shooting.

sites.name: Coon Island Conservation Area
sites.description: MDC-managed 3,223-acre bottomland wetland area on the Black River just north of the Arkansas line, south of Poplar Bluff. This pin is the area's south boat ramp: a concrete ramp on the main river with primitive campsites, a privy and accessible facilities. It is the last public ramp before Arkansas. The area floods often and parts of it close for waterfowl from mid-October to March 1.
sites.facilities: Concrete boat ramp, designated primitive camping area, privy, disabled-accessible facilities (per MDC area map icons and ramp layer). Gravel road and turnaround visible at the ramp. Self check-in stations for hunters at the area parking lots.
sites.parking_info: Gravel turnaround and parking at the ramp and campground (visible in aerial imagery). MDC's area map marks its numbered parking lots elsewhere on the area, not at this site. Capacity not published.
sites.road_access: MDC's published directions to the area are: from Poplar Bluff, take Highway 53 south, then Route HH south 8 miles, then County Road 244 east 1 mile. That route reaches the north parking lots and the north ramp, NOT this pin. The south ramp is at the end of a short gravel spur running north from Butler County Road 249, about 0.4 mile west of where CR 249 meets CR 240 and CR 245 at the south end of the area (MDC area map; OSM/TIGER roads). The turn-by-turn route from Route HH to CR 249 is not confirmed.
sites.fee_notes: No fee is listed on the MDC area page or brochure. MDC conservation areas do not charge entry fees.
sites.local_tips:
Area open 4 a.m. to 10 p.m. Launching and landing boats, fishing and camping are allowed 24 hours. Waterfowl Refuge zones are closed to all use Oct 15 to Mar 1. Waterfowl-Hunting-Only zones are closed to other users from Oct 15 to the end of duck season. Camping only in designated areas, 14 consecutive days in any 30-day period. Boats may not be left unattended overnight. No swimming. Nontoxic shot only. MDC advises calling the Otter Slough CA office (573-624-5821) before a trip because water levels change a lot with the river.

MDC's 2004 watershed angler guide names the Coon Island area as one of the two best places on the Black River for large spotted bass.

The other (OBJECTID 99, 36.56169,-90.35021, ADA No) is about 6.7 river miles upstream near the CR 244 parking lots. A qualifier stops users and reviewers from mixing them up. sites.name: Rocky Creek Conservation Area
sites.description: MDC gravel-bar launch on the west (river-right) bank of the Current River, about a mile below the NPS Powder Mill access and on the opposite bank from it, roughly across from the Blue Spring area inside the Ozark National Scenic Riverways corridor. sites.name: Dalton Boat Ramp

sites.name: Pacific Palisades Conservation Area
sites.description: MDC conservation area of 695 acres just east of Pacific, with about 3 miles of lower Meramec River frontage. The concrete boat ramp is on the north (St. Louis County) bank off Franklin Road, not on the Jefferson County side. Start here for Pacific Palisades to Allenton (about 7 mi) or Route 66 State Park (about 13 mi) floats. Two old gravel-pit lakes connect to the river only at high water.

reach_context.character: Lowland big river, not an Ozark float. The Black leaves the Ozark border at Poplar Bluff and here meanders through flat Mississippi Alluvial Plain bottomland hardwood and cypress-tupelo swamp. It has very low gradient, fine sand and silt banks, turbid water, high mud banks and no riffles or gravel bars to speak of. It is regulated upstream by Corps of Engineers releases from Clearwater Lake (MO). Effectively flatwater with current (no whitewater class). Above Datto the river splits: the Black keeps the Datto channel and Little River (fed through the Swift Ditch diversion) loops east past Hubble Bridge; the two rejoin about 1.1 miles above Brookings. Mainly used by motorboats, anglers (catfish, crappie, bass) and duck hunters; paddlers are rare. Rough float legs at about 2 mph paddling: Datto to Brookings 6.7 mi (3-4 hr), Brookings to Schaeffer's Eddy 11.2 mi (5-6 hr), Schaeffer's Eddy to Pocahontas city ramp about 22.9 mi (a full day or more, passing the Current River confluence about 16.7 mi down).
reach_context.hazards: Flooding: overbank floods are frequent and long, and the WMA's levees, roads and ramps go under (NWS Corning flood stage 15 ft; 17 ft floods Brookings). Strainers and debris: the master plan notes reduced flow, sedimentation and debris drifts between the Swift Ditch confluence and Datto; downed timber is common throughout. Swift Ditch weir: AGFC installed a weir in the mid-1980s to push water into Little River. It once dropped the Black too low for boats between Swift Ditch and Datto; it has since been lowered, but its exact location (upstream of Datto) is unconfirmed, so paddlers starting above Datto must scout it. Little River Dam: a 6-bay gated dam (about 36.316,-90.697, gates installed around Oct. 15 each year) on Little River upstream of Hubble Bridge; avoid the Little River channel above Hubble. Water-control siphon intakes ('Upper Siphon') sit at the Black River bank near the Peach Orchard gauge (about mile 163.4); keep clear. Motorboat traffic: AGFC calls boating its biggest safety hazard, with a pre-dawn 'rush hour' of hunter boats in duck season (WMA open 2-4 a.m. closures, hunters off the water by noon). Hunting: WMA deer archery Sept. 26-Feb. 28, modern-gun permit hunt Nov. 14-18, waterfowl, dove, turkey. Remote with few exits, poor cell coverage likely (unverified), heavy mosquitoes, biting flies and poison ivy (AGFC). No published paddling-level thresholds exist for any gauge on this reach.

reach_context.character: Below Poplar Bluff the Black leaves the Ozarks for the Mississippi Alluvial Plain (the Bootheel lowlands). For about the first 10 miles it is mildly sinuous, with a narrow forested strip and levees generally within 0.25 mile of both banks. Farther down it meanders more and the forest corridor widens to about 0.5 mile (USGS SIR 2021-5067). Gradient falls to about 1 ft/mile, and 0.6 ft/mile at the state line (MDC 2004 watershed inventory). The water is slow and sand- or silt-bedded: no riffles, no gravel bars of the Ozark kind, and no rapids. This is flatwater paddling where wind and current speed set travel time, not a spring-fed Ozark float. Around Coon Island CA the river runs in two parallel channels (OSM), and Swift Ditch parallels the river nearby (NRCS 2025). Public accesses are few and far apart: Sportsman's Park, then Dan River (about 8 mi), then the Coon Island north ramp (about 18.6 mi farther, western channel), then the Coon Island south ramp (about 21.3 mi from Dan River on the main channel). After that there is nothing confirmed until Arkansas. These are concrete ramps also used by fishing boats. Spotted bass, catfish and white bass fishery.
reach_context.hazards: 1) Flooding and levee breaches. The levee system between Poplar Bluff and the state line breached in 2008, 2011, 2017 and 2024 (NRCS Federal Register notice, 2025). When the river is high, the floodplain between the levees goes under, and so do the access roads and ramps. Coon Island CA floods often, and MDC warns of unexpected deep water when it is flooded. 2) Clearwater Dam flood-control releases can hold the river high for long periods after rain upstream. Releases are timed to the Poplar Bluff stage. 3) Long, remote stretches with few take-outs and levees blocking the view inland; an early exit is hard. 4) Channel splits around Coon Island (two parallel channels, plus Swift Ditch nearby). NRCS has proposed a low-water weir to push Swift Ditch flow back into the main river and channel cleanout from above Hargrove Pivot Bridge to the Arkansas border, which suggests problems with how flow splits and with channel capacity. Paddlers should stay in the main channel. 5) Expect strainers and woody debris, as on any forested lowland river. No source specific to this reach was found, so treat this as general rather than verified. 6) Motorboat traffic: all ramps are concrete and MDC areas allow boats and motors. 7) Waterfowl-season closures on parts of Coon Island CA from Oct 15 to Mar 1. 8) Bridges: CR 159 (OSM: CR 658) (Hargrove Pivot Bridge, about 7.3 mi below Dan River) was closed to traffic in 2021 for structural problems; current status unknown. There is also a CR 214 bridge near the north end of Coon Island. Neither is a designated access.

reach_context.character: Below Doniphan the Current leaves the Ozark Highlands and becomes a broad, slower, sand-and-gravel lowland river, and it is described as silt-laden by the time it enters Arkansas. In Arkansas it forms the boundary between the Ozark Plateau and the Mississippi Alluvial Plain. Spring water keeps flows relatively steady. It is Class I flatwater, with large islands (Big Island, Float Missouri mile 129.8) and a lake-like pool (Goose Lake, mile 135.0) above the state line. The Little Black River joins from the northeast about 9 mi below the state line, near Datto. Trip distances: Deer Leap to T. L. Wright about 6.5 mi; Float Camp to T. L. Wright about 5.5 mi (the standard Doniphan tube/canoe float). T. L. Wright to the state line is about 14 mi. T. L. Wright to Johnston's Eddy is about 29-31 mi (multi-day). Johnston's Eddy to the Black River confluence is about 20 mi, and the confluence to the Pocahontas city ramp on the Black is about 6.3 mi more. River crossings below Doniphan per OSM: US 160 (Doniphan), AR 328 (near Reyno), an abandoned Frisco rail bridge, and US 62/67 (near Biggers, about 10.6 mi below Johnston's Eddy).
reach_context.hazards: No dams or weirs on the segment. Motorboats are common below Doniphan, per Mark Twain NF, which also says the Doniphan stretch gets crowded on hot summer weekends. Mark Twain NF currently warns that recent flooding left trees, root wads and strainers in the Current River. Islands and side channels in the lowland reach can split flow; Goose Lake is a slow, wind-exposed pool. Flooding: Doniphan flood stage (minor) is 13 ft. Expect long stretches of private land in Arkansas with few legal stops beyond gravel bars; one canoe-club forum says banks are heavily posted, which is anecdotal and unverified, since that host could not be fetched. Levee locations in the Arkansas alluvial reach were not researched or confirmed.

reach_context.character: A spring-fed Ozark river carrying Missouri's Greer Spring flow. It stays floatable year-round, is Class I, and its water is clear and cool (an outfitter cites about 69-74°F in summer). Below the Missouri scenic-river corridor it becomes wider and slower, running through farmland with gravel bars, shoals, islands and many downed trees. Smallmouth bass and spring walleye are the main fish, with largemouth and catfish lower down. Public access is very sparse. Road access is public only at Myrtle (MO), Dalton (AR 93) and the AGFC Eleven Point River Access near US 62. Other road crossings are the Hwy 90 bridge (USGS gauge) and the Blacks Ferry Road bridge. River miles from the OSM line: Myrtle to Dalton about 11.0; Dalton to the AR 93 bridge 0.3; Dalton to the Hwy 90 bridge about 9.1; Hwy 90 to the Blacks Ferry bridge about 6.4; Blacks Ferry to the Eleven Point River Access about 4.5; Eleven Point River Access to the US 62 bridge about 0.6; US 62 to the Spring River confluence about 10.5. The common commercial floats are 4-14 mi between private outfitter put-ins and take-outs. A 1998 Arkansas guide calls the river above Dalton reasonably safe for most at low-medium water, and below Dalton unsuitable for inexperienced paddlers because of the old stone dams.
reach_context.hazards: 1) Old rock/stone dams. A 1997-98 Arkansas guide lists five between MO 142 and the mouth: one about 6-7 mi below MO 142 (in MO, above Myrtle or near the line); one at Dalton just above the AR 93 bridge (aerial imagery shows a riffle line there right below the ramp); one about 8 mi below Dalton just above the Hwy 90 bridge; one just above US 62; and one a few miles below US 62. They are dangerous at high water, and paddlers should line or portage through the chutes. Their current condition is unverified. 2) Strainers: many downed trees are left in the river as fish habitat (2021 trip report). 3) Collapsing gravel bars, debris jams and islands that can block channels. 4) Swift current at the AR 93 bridge, and steep banks with deep water at the Blacks Ferry bridge (1998 guide). 5) Flooding: NWS RVSA4 flood stage is 15 ft. Stay off at high water. 6) Mostly private land along the banks: gravel-bar camping and stops need care, and there is no public camping. 7) No dams or Corps releases. The proposed Water Valley dam was never built, and the Corps recommended de-authorizing it in 1965. The AGFC concrete ramps also serve trailered motorboats, so occasional jon boats are possible. 8) No cell service on the Dalton-to-Stubblefield stretch.

reach_context.character: A big, low-gradient river through the urban and suburban edge of the St. Louis metro, in a Class I setting. Wide channel with long pools, gravel bars and beaches, scattered riffles, and bluffs at Pacific Palisades and Castlewood. The I-44 corridor and railroads run alongside, with houses and debris along some banks. A paddler's log notes 'cars, trash, broken bridges' for a few miles. Typical day trips: Pacific Palisades to Allenton about 7 mi; Allenton to Route 66 SP about 7-8 mi; Pacific Palisades to Route 66 SP about 13 mi; Route 66 SP to Valley Park about 13 mi (6-7 h). A group-paddle organizer reports current as far as Castlewood, small rapids at Glencoe, and slack 'dead water' for the last ~3 miles above Valley Park. Fishing boats, jet boats and jet skis use the ramps, and State Parks maps list motorized boat traffic as a river hazard. Flows are much larger than on Eddy's upper Meramec: about 400-500 cfs at late-October 2026 base flow, and over 100,000 cfs in the 2015 and 2017 floods.
reach_context.hazards: (1) Flooding: the lower Meramec floods quickly and hard. Record crests came in Dec 2015 and May 2017 (Eureka 46.1 ft and 169,000 cfs; Valley Park 44.1 ft; Pacific 33.4 ft). The Corps-built Valley Park levee held in 2008 and came close to overtopping in 2015 but held. Meramec Landing and the other ramps sit riverward and go under early. Use the NWS action stages (Pacific 13 ft, Eureka 17 ft, Valley Park 11 ft) as a 'do not float' guide. (2) Strainers and logjams: Castlewood SP describes logjams and root wads, and a 2013 log reports a tree blocking a side channel above Allenton. Side channels around islands below Pacific Palisades are where blockages collect. (3) Motorboat and jet-ski traffic on this big-water reach, especially below Castlewood and near the Valley Park, Greentree and George Winter ramps. (4) Swimming deaths: the Castlewood plan's public comments repeatedly mention drownings and strong current off the park's beaches. Brochures prohibit swimming at Pacific Palisades. (5) Water quality: Kiefer Creek, which enters at Castlewood, is on Missouri's 303(d) list for E. coli (East-West Gateway lower Meramec watershed plan). Avoid water contact, especially after rain. Missouri has a long-standing lead 'do not eat' advisory for sunfish, carp and suckers from the Big River, which enters between Allenton and Route 66 SP. No source found extends it to the Meramec main stem. (6) Times Beach: Route 66 State Park is the former town of Times Beach, evacuated in 1983 for dioxin (TCDD) contamination and later cleaned up and made into the park. It is history, not a current paddling hazard, but users ask about it. (7) No dams or weirs were found on the Pacific to Valley Park reach. The dam remnants in search results are on the Big River tributary. Bridge piers at Pacific, I-44, Hwy 109, Route 66 and Hwy 141 can catch debris. (8) Route 66 SP gates close at a set time and no longer let cars out automatically, so take out before gate closure.

suggested_section.notes: Pacific Palisades to Valley Park by Eddy geometry is 26.9 mi, which matches the paddler figures (13 + 13). Eddy's existing 'Lower Meramec (below Meramec State Park)' section has no bounds or gauge. Consider splitting it into (a) Meramec SP to Robertsville (existing approved accesses; Sullivan 07014500), (b) Robertsville to Pacific (Pacific gauge 07017020; long ~39 mi gap with only the seasonal Catawissa CA ramp), and (c) this section. The reach below Valley Park (Greentree, George Winter, Arnold) is wide, slow, powerboat-oriented water best left out for now.

Catawissa Conservation Area (MDC area 7853), Franklin County, between Robertsville and Pacific. Boat ramp on an old gravel-pit lake that connects to the Meramec only at higher water: MDC calls it a seasonal access. Directions: north of Catawissa on Route N, then east on Frisco Drive. OSM slipway 'Backwater' 12773240798 at 38.4444847,-90.7675196; How's Your River 38.44449353,-90.76751295. It was not in the candidate list. Worth adding with a 'high water only' note, since it is the only public site in the ~39-mile Robertsville to Pacific gap. Source: https://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/places/catawissa-conservation-area

Castlewood State Park, Ballwin. No designated public boat ramp is listed. Missouri State Parks lists river access 'at numerous spots along River Scene, Stinging Nettle and Al Foster trails'. The 2024 Conceptual Development Plan mentions an 'existing gravel boat launch' on the peninsula, to be rebuilt for EMS/first-responder use, and a planned canoe/kayak access about 220 yards SE of the Glencoe (Al Foster) trailhead. OSM has a gravel 'Walk In' slipway at 38.5347277,-90.5887014. Not recommended until the public status of a launch is confirmed. Sources: https://mostateparks.com/park/castlewood/fishing ; https://mostateparks.com/sites/g/files/zuston361/files/media/pdf/2024/11/Castlewood_CDP_Final.pdf

Al Foster Memorial Trailhead, Glencoe (City of Wildwood). OSM slipway 'Foster Trail' 2594478772 at 38.5412046,-90.624114 (gravel, note 'Walk In', access=yes). A carry-down only, unconfirmed by the city. Between Route 66 SP and Castlewood.
Sherman Beach Park (St. Louis County), near Castlewood. A popular gravel beach and Greenway trailhead (OSM 38.548,-90.597). No source confirms a boat launch. Not recommended as a launch.

Greentree Park, Kirkwood: river boat ramp per Great Rivers Greenway ('launch your boat on the Meramec River at the boat ramps in Meramec Landing Park and Greentree Park'). OSM unnamed slipway 3335175137 at 38.5584476,-90.4479996. It is about 3 km BELOW Valley Park, outside the suggested section. Source: https://greatriversgreenway.org/greenways/meramec-greenway-greentree-park-to-arnolds-grove-park

George Winter Park, Fenton (St. Louis County). Concrete river ramps per Great Rivers Greenway; OSM slipways 497387836 (fee=yes) at 38.5033542,-90.4217449 and 497387837 at 38.5016668,-90.4206832. An undated third-party listing cites a $5 per watercraft daily fee. Below Valley Park, outside the section. The county page was blocked by a Cloudflare challenge.

gauges.name: Big Piney River near Simmons, MO
gauges.notes: Located exactly at Simmons Ford (37.24167,-92.00972) but holds only a single 2006-07-31 field visit. Not a gauge.

reach_context.character: Small headwater Ozark stream. Missouri Ozark Waterways (MDC, via floatmissouri.com) rates the Big Piney Class I, seldom II except in high water, but starts its mile-by-mile at Baptist Camp (mile 0.0, 'Low-water bridge. No ramp.'). Southwest Paddler starts at Simmons Ford (0.0) with Baptist Camp at about 1.7 mi, Dog's Bluff (Hwy 17) at about 10.7 mi, and Mineral Springs at about 15.6 mi. It says flow is almost always adequate below Dog's Bluff, but the upper 10.6 miles 'may be very low in normal conditions' and are paddled after heavy local rainfall. Simmons Ford → Baptist Camp is a very short trip (about 1.7–1.9 mi). Most paddlers would continue to Dog's Bluff (about 10.7 mi from Simmons Ford).
reach_context.hazards: Very low water and dragging most of the year. The low-water bridge at Baptist Camp is a pinning/strainer hazard at higher flows. US 63 bridge piers at the put-in. The river rises rapidly after rain (USFS Big Piney page, lower river). Logjams and strainers are typical of small Ozark streams but not specifically documented here.

reach_context.segment: Joe Crighton Access → Delaware Town Access (upper/urban reach; about 20 river miles)

gauges.name: James River near Springfield, MO
gauges.notes: At the FR 164 (Kinser) bridge, the south end of Joe Crighton Access (37.14997,-93.20339; OSM monitoring_station node 12092128270; NWS SGFM7). Active: 4.56 cfs / 3.57 ft at 2026-10-29 00:00 CDT, far too low to float. Eddy's dossier records moherp OBSERVED Low 40 / Good 150 / Flood 1400 cfs on this gauge. It represents Crighton → Lake Springfield directly. It is also the best available proxy for Kissick dam → Delaware Town, because Wilson Creek only enters about 1.8 mi above Delaware Town (MOW mile 25.2), though dam operations affect that reach.

gauges.name: James River near Boaz, MO
gauges.notes: 56.3 cfs at 2026-10-28 23:45 CDT. Below Wilson Creek; Eddy uses it for the Delaware Town / Shelvin Rock / Hootentown reach. Not representative above Lake Springfield.

reach_context.character: Class I upper Ozark stream draining Springfield's east and south sides. MOW notes 'a few places on upper river rate up to III due to obstructions'. Its gradient runs 6.3 ft/mi from Hwy 125 to Lake Springfield and 4.3 ft/mi from the dam to Hwy 14. MOW miles: Hwy 125/McCraw Ford 0.0; Joe Crighton 6.8; Hwy 60 bridge 9.5, where the lake backwater begins; Southwood Access 10.0; Lake Springfield (about 2 mi); public park/boathouse access 12.1; dam 12.3; Tailwaters Access 12.4; Hwy 160 bridge 15.8 ('fair access'); Owens Bridge 18.7; rock-ledge shoal 20.3 ('Walk or line!'); Delaware Town 27.0; Hwy 14 bridge access 27.5. The established paddle is the 6-mile James River Water Trail, Crighton → Lake Springfield Park boathouse (Ozark Greenways; Class I at normal levels; daylight only; do not use in flood). Boathouse rentals run spring through fall.
reach_context.hazards: LAKE SPRINGFIELD DAM. On 2026-06-14 four family members went over it while floating; three died. City Utilities says warning signs and buoys sit about 100 ft upstream. In September 2026 CU closed the Tailwaters Access below the dam indefinitely ('permanently closed' per a CU rep quoted by KY3), citing dangerous tailwater hydraulics, so there is now no open public put-in at the dam and no published portage. The dam was built for the now-retired James River Power Station. Other hazards: a 2-mile flatwater lake crossing; the rock-ledge shoal with brush and logs at MOW mile 20.3; deadfall and overhanging limbs between the dam/Hwy 160 and Delaware Town with multiple portages at low water (anecdotal r/springfieldMO, 2025); flashy urban runoff; frequent very low summer flow (4–5 cfs at Springfield today).

suggested_section.name: James River Water Trail (Joe Crighton → Lake Springfield Park boathouse)
suggested_section.end_access: Lake Springfield Park boathouse launch (Springfield-Greene County Park Board; not yet in Eddy)
suggested_section.notes: End the section at the boathouse, the last public take-out above the dam. Do NOT define a continuous section from Crighton to Delaware Town through the dam. A separate below-dam section (Hwy 160 bridge → Delaware Town, about 11 mi) would need a verified legal put-in first. NOTE: Eddy's existing upper section is named 'Upper / urban reach (Hwy 125 → Hootentown)', but no approved access exists above Delaware Town, and the name implies a through-route across the dam. Recommend renaming it.

gauges.name: Mulberry River near Mulberry, AR
gauges.notes: 0.88 ft / 8.8 cfs at 2026-10-28 23:30 CDT (unfloatable). USFS: 'Readings between 2.0 and 4.0 are ideal, while 4.5 and beyond are considered dangerous'. USFS doesn't name the gauge, but American Whitewater ties its Mulberry reports to this gauge. Southwest Paddler gives a finer stage ladder: below 1.6 ft very low; 1.6–1.9 beginner; 2.4–2.9 intermediate; 4.7–4.9 no rentals; 5+ unsafe. Southwest Paddler also cites a separate 'SH 23 gauge at Turner Bend' for low-water-bridge clearance.

reach_context.character: Wild and Scenic, seasonal Ozark whitewater stream, Class I–II (II–III at higher stages). Usually floated late fall to June. Gradient about 15 fpm Wolf Pen–Redding and 12 fpm Redding–Hwy 23. AR 215 parallels the river on the north side.
reach_context.hazards: Fast rises after rain; willow strainers and downed trees; ledges and standing waves. CR 1504 low-water bridge about 3.4 mi below Indian Creek (Southwest Paddler: no left-side clearance, duck far right) is a serious hazard between Indian Creek and Redding.
